chunks: Ḥanān narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: I heard him saying, 'A man came to Abū Dharr and gave him good news of his sheep that had given birth. He said, “O Abū Dharr, I bring glad tidings that your sheep have reproduced and increased in number!” He said, “I am not pleased by their increase in number. The few of them that are sufficient are more beloved to me than many that distract [me]. Verily I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: On the two sides of the path (ṣirāt) on the Day of Judgment will be the near of kin and the trusts, so when one who kept ties with the near of kin and returned the trusts passes by them, they will not throw him into the Fire.”'

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abū Dharr, a companion of the Prophet known for his asceticism
key_terms.الرَّحِم: Kinship/relatives, specifically the bond of family ties
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The path over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْأَمَانَةُ: Trusts, referring to duties and obligations owed to God and others
key_terms.الْمُوَصِّلُ لِلرَّحِم: One who maintains ties of kinship
key_terms.يَتَكَافَبَا: They throw him (dual form, referring to Kinship and Trusts)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of kinship and trusts on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights Abū Dharr’s ascetic preference for sufficiency over abundance, grounded in the eschatological significance of maintaining kinship ties (ṣilat al-raḥim) and fulfilling trusts (al-amānah). In Shia tradition, these two virtues are viewed as the primary criteria for divine mercy, with the Prophet (ṣ) indicating that those who uphold them will be spared the 'tossing' into Hellfire, emphasizing their role as protective shields on the Day of Judgment.
